beats.narration: Google calls this model E4B: effectively four billion parameters. Its weights add up to about eight. Where did the other four go?
beats.narration_text: Gemma 3n E4B: (1) explain how the E2B model is nested inside E4B, (2) show me how per-layer embeddings move parameters off the accelerator, (3) compute the size of the per-layer embedding table from config.json.

props.command: Gemma 3n E4B: (1) explain how the E2B model is nested inside E4B, (2) show me how per-layer embeddings move parameters off the accelerator, (3) compute the size of the per-layer embedding table from config.json.
output: NEST      E2B = 30 of 35 layers · half-width FFN
EFFECTIVE ≈ what must sit in accelerator memory

beats.narration: A smaller model nested inside a bigger one, plus a lookup table that can live off the accelerator. The nesting, the table, the label.
beats.narration_text: A smaller model nested inside a bigger one, plus a lookup table that can live off the accelerator. The nesting, the table, the label.

props.title: Gemma 3n, Four Billion or Eight?
thesis: Gemma 3n E4B nests a smaller E2B model inside its own weights, and keeps
2.35B per-layer embedding parameters where they can be cached off the accelerator.

roadmap.label: The nesting
roadmap.body: E2B is 30 of E4B's 35 layers, at half the FFN width.

roadmap.label: The label
roadmap.body: 'E4B' is a memory load, not a parameter count.

props.source: Google, Gemma 3n docs · gemma-3n-E4B-it / E2B-it config.json

beats.narration: This is MatFormer, a Matryoshka transformer. The E2B model lives inside E4B: thirty of thirty-five layers, half the feed-forward width. Train once, extract either.
beats.narration_text: This is MatFormer, a Matryoshka transformer. The E2B model lives inside E4B: thirty of thirty-five layers, half the feed-forward width. Train once, extract either.

props.spark: Two models, one set of weights.
props.heading: MatFormer — E2B lives inside E4B

moves.label: E2B
moves.detail: 30 layers · feed-forward width 8,192 — a subset of E4B's own weights.

moves.label: ATTENTION
moves.detail: Both: 4 sliding-window layers (512 tokens) to every 1 global layer.

moves.label: INPUTS
moves.detail: Text, plus a MobileNet-V5 vision encoder and an audio encoder.

props.keepNote: Row 2 is the trick: the small model isn't a second model — it is part of the big one.
props.source: config.json, E4B vs E2B: num_hidden_layers 35 vs 30 · intermediate_size 16384 vs 8192 · Google, Gemma 3n docs (MatFormer)

beats.narration: Second trick: per-layer embeddings. Each of the thirty-five layers gets its own small vector per token. Those are lookups, not matrix multiplies, so they can be cached off the accelerator.
beats.narration_text: Second trick: per-layer embeddings. Each of the thirty-five layers gets its own small vector per token. Those are lookups, not matrix multiplies, so they can be cached off the accelerator.

props.heading: Per-layer embeddings (PLE)

moves.label: INPUT
moves.detail: One 2,048-number embedding per token, at the input — as usual.

moves.label: PER LAYER
moves.detail: Each of the 35 layers also gets its own 256-number vector for that token.

moves.label: LOOKUP
moves.detail: Table rows, not matrix multiplies: they can be cached on CPU or fast storage.

props.keepNote: Row 3 is why it matters: a lookup can wait in slower memory until its layer runs.
props.source: gemma-3n-E4B-it config.json: vocab_size_per_layer_input 262144 · hidden_size_per_layer_input 256 · Google, Gemma 3n docs (PLE caching)

beats.narration: Now the label. E4B ships eight point four billion parameters. Two point three five billion of them are that lookup table. And Google's own figure for E2B: over five billion loaded, one point nine one effective.
beats.narration_text: Now the label. E4B ships eight point four billion parameters. Two point three five billion of them are that lookup table. And Google's own figure for E2B: over five billion loaded, one point nine one effective.

props.heading: Parameters — billions
props.exception: The dashed line is the 4 in “E4B”. Effective means memory load — all 8.4B still ship, and still run.
props.source: safetensors index totals: E4B 8,387,373,392 · E2B 5,976,833,472 · E2B 1.91B: Gemma 3n docs, Fig. 1

beats.narration: Verdict: the nesting is real, and a big slice of the weights can live off the accelerator. But effective four billion is a memory budget, not a parameter count.
beats.narration_text: Verdict: the nesting is real, and a big slice of the weights can live off the accelerator. But effective four billion is a memory budget, not a parameter count.

artifactLines: Nesting: E2B is a 30-layer, half-width subset of E4B's weights (MatFormer).
PLE: ~2.35B of E4B's 8.39B parameters are per-layer lookups that can be cached off the accelerator.
Effective: a memory load — Google's E2B figure is 1.91B effective, of over 5B loaded.
Read 'E' numbers as memory budgets, not parameter counts.
props.sourceNote: Google, Gemma 3n docs · gemma-3n-E4B-it / E2B-it config.json + safetensors index

beats.narration: Your turn. Run E4B next to a plain four billion model on one laptop. Record accelerator memory, CPU memory, and speed. Did the memory just move?
beats.narration_text: Run Gemma 3n E4B and a plain 4B model on the same laptop. Record peak accelerator memory, peak CPU memory and tokens per second for a 2,000-token prompt. Then compare accuracy on 50 questions. Is 'effective 4B' a fair label on memory, speed and quality?

props.command: Run Gemma 3n E4B and a plain 4B model on the same laptop. Record peak accelerator memory, peak CPU memory and tokens per second for a 2,000-token prompt. Then compare accuracy on 50 questions. Is 'effective 4B' a fair label on memory, speed and quality?
output: FLAG   the memory just moved to CPU

beats.narration: Four billion, or eight? Both. That was Gemma three n.
